artifact.canonical_name: Towards Intelligent Computation Offloading in Dynamic Vehicular Networks: A Scalable Multilayer Pipeline

sources.title: Towards Intelligent Computation Offloading in Dynamic Vehicular Networks: A Scalable Multilayer Pipeline
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors propose a four-layer computation-offloading pipeline that distributes vehicular functions to cloud/edge resources while enforcing round-trip-time requirements.
An enhanced particle-swarm optimization incorporates vehicle distance/direction and functional requirements for mobile edge-server selection.
A Kubernetes-based cloud evaluation with realistic mobility patterns is reported to reduce average response time versus brute-force while maintaining latency-critical task success rate.

metrics.name: reported average PSO execution time for ten servers/tasks
metrics.context: CPU case reported in the primary abstract.

metrics.name: reported execution time for 15 servers and 1000 tasks
metrics.context: GPU case reported in the primary abstract.

limitations.text: The accessible primary abstract does not expose round-trip-time thresholds, mobility traces, task workloads, brute-force search budget, response-time values, success-rate values, or offloading-network assumptions.
The work motivates safety-critical workloads but the abstract does not establish a safety case for offloading safety-critical control functions.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Towards Intelligent Computation Offloading in Dynamic Vehicular Networks: A Scalable Multilayer Pipeline; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary abstract verifies the four-layer architecture, enhanced PSO, Kubernetes/mobility evaluation and 26-ms/550-ms optimizer figures, but detailed system/evaluation constraints remain unresolved.

unresolved_questions: Inspect full paper for RTT constraints, function classes, network/mobility model, response-time and success-rate results, baseline complexity, and safety boundary.

editorial.why_now_note: Cloud/edge offloading extends the SDV compute-placement boundary beyond the vehicle, making connectivity/latency part of function-allocation architecture.
editorial.rationale: Potentially important cloud-to-edge evidence, but strong offloading claims and the 26/550-ms optimizer figures need full context before editorial promotion.
